divergence: Hollywood was never founded — the film capital of the world is Fort Lee, New Jersey, and the stars ride the PATH train
story_angle: man-on-the-street reactions to a rumor that the missing thing might exist somewhere, treated like a UFO sighting
headline: PATH Train Riders Report Rival Film Studios Spoiling Commuter Calm
deck: Local transit authorities brace for cinematic invasion as bureaucratic safeguards mount against phantom California productions.
article:
Fort Lee commuters filed police reports this week after an anonymous tip claimed rival studios in California were leaking scripts onto PATH cars. The Fort Lee Film Commission responded by slapping a 25% surcharge on any fare that mentions "Hollywood West," unless the rider signs a notarized "no California contact" affidavit.

Tom B. Hargrove said a page reading "Santa Monica" blew past him at Journal Square. "I don't want palm trees ruining my daily commute," he told officers. The Transit Bureau widened its threat list to cover any reference to "west of the Hudson" and now stamps every ticket with a pre-approval code.

Actors must submit written proof of New Jersey loyalty before boarding. Non-compliant agents pay double the surcharge. Office worker Susan L. Gibbons clutched her coffee and asked why a celebrity now needs a travel advisor just to ride the PATH.

Scriptwriting classes have seen a spike in enrollment while riders report "mysterious drones" overhead, possibly scouting auditions. The Bureau of Cinematic Integrity has tightened passenger checks, leaving commuters to navigate a Hollywood-free morning routine.
author: Patricia R. Trainwell, Senior Transit Correspondent

oped.title: PATH Riders Should Thank the Studios for the Free Glamour Upgrade
oped.author: Reginald F. Swank, Emeritus Professor of Cinematic Commuting at the Fort Lee Institute of Unmade Masterpieces
oped.body: The supposed crisis on the PATH amounts to commuters complaining about their quiet time while local productions bring actual star power into the tunnels. Riders who dislike megaphones and smoke machines should first consider their own drab clothing, which wrecks every shot. Mandatory screen tests at Journal Square would solve the problem: failures can walk the bridge like the extras they are. This protects the industry and clears my car of the passenger whose fedora keeps photobombing my close-ups. Progress requires sacrifice, preferably from everyone else.

classifieds.text: Selling slightly dented PATH train seats repurposed as director chairs after rival crews turned my morning commute into a car chase. First $800 takes them—call Fort Lee before the 6:12 derails my marriage.

NJ Pictures needs unflappable commuters for crowd scenes that won't escalate into actual fistfights with California scouts. Must own noise-canceling headphones and a tolerance for fog machines on moving trains.
Lost: one fog machine and my dignity on the PATH after a rival crew hijacked car 3 for an impromptu car chase. Reward if returned before transit cops ticket me for "unauthorized cinema."

Public notice: Fort Lee Studios apologizes for the spontaneous musical number that halted the 7:45 to 33rd St yesterday. All future productions will now require pre-approved scripts and zero tap-dancing on third rails.

panels.caption: PATH rider to conductor: "That Fort Lee Pictures creep just screamed the 'Jersey Heist' ending at me."
Transit chief: "We're screening every passenger for fake LA press badges and phony script leaks."
Rider, smirking: "Too late. The rival studio already filmed my reaction for their next trailer."

stories.headline: Film Producers Absorb PATH Fare Hikes After Manifest Rules Take Effect
stories.deck: Accounting departments track every delay as rival crews board the same cars.
stories.article:
Fort Lee studios now bill line producers for the new manifest surcharges. One action picture added a line item called "train coordination" that covers both fares and overtime for crews delayed by competing stars.

Two rival productions share the same morning run and route call times through a neutral scheduler to avoid accidental set collisions. The extra paperwork prevents the half-day shutdown that occurred when one crew's early arrival tipped off the other.

stories.headline: Palisades HOA Votes to Limit Red-Carpet Foot Traffic
stories.deck: Residents cite wear on sidewalks and blocked driveways during evening premieres.
stories.article:
The Edgewater Palisades Homeowners Association capped red-carpet events at three evenings a month after complaints about idling limousines and delivery trucks. President Linda Voss said the limit applies to every studio along the cliff.

Productions must file a traffic plan ten days ahead. Fines now scale with the number of stars listed on the PATH manifest, a clause added after one resident counted seventeen limousines at a single July premiere.
